Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Raleigh NC
201 PM EDT Sat Oct 24 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

* Nothing appreciable.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 115 PM Saturday... 

1) The persistent pattern of dry and largely seasonable weather will 
continue through next week. 


&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 115 PM Saturday... 

KEY MESSAGE 1... The persistent pattern of dry and largely 
seasonable weather will continue through next week. 

The mid and upper level weather pattern will feature high amplitude 
upper level ridge extending from the western Gulf north into the 
western Great Lakes with a general northerly flow across the 
Carolinas through Monday. The ridge will weaken and flatten as it 
slowly shifts east reaching the eastern U.S. coast by early in the 
weekend. Moisture-starved disturbances will move near or across our 
area early Sunday morning and Wednesday night with little impact. 

At the surface, high pressure centered over New England today will 
shift south into the mid Atlantic for Sunday and Monday. A 
reinforcing Canadian high will build into the region for Wednesday 
and Thursday with potentially another surface high extending into 
our region for Saturday. 

It's worth noting that as the ridge flattens and shifts east late 
in the week/weekend and the flow becomes more westerly and even 
southwesterly, deep layer moisture will increase somewhat resulting 
in more clouds. There will also be the need to consider limited 
non-zero rain chances late next weekend into early next week. 

&&

.AVIATION /18Z SATURDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
As of 200 PM Saturday...

24 hour TAF period: VFR conditions should largely prevail through 
the next 24 hours. Stratocumulus clouds should persist across the 
area through the weekend, with cloud bases generally above 3 kft and 
few to scattered in coverage. However, brief periods of MVFR stratus 
are possible again early Sun morning, mainly at KINT and KGSO. 
Expect nely winds to prevail, with occasional gusts into the teens 
to 20 kts with daytime heating today and Sun. 

Outlook: Aside from the aforementioned small chance of sub-VFR 
ceilings in nely flow this weekend, dry, VFR conditions are expected 
to persist for at least the next several days. 

&&

.RAH WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&
